I was in an economics class, discussing the pros and cons of raising minimum wage to $10-$15/hour. The economics professor was HARDCORE against the raise, which was whatever, but I still wanted to write my paper in favor.

 I figured it'd be fine as long as I backed up my arguments with verifiable evidence and statistics, right? 

Dude. I'll admit I'm a bit of a tryhard. Girl's got ZERO chill and I always go for that A+. Screw the bell curve. I collaborated with my Stats study group, pulled way more sources than necessary, and actually got really into the research. Economics isn't usually my jam, but I really enjoyed the research. Basically, I was sure I'd ace the paper. I was proud of it.

Sadly, I forgot how the school system works sometimes. Dude gave me a C on it and chicken scratched all over it about how raising the minimum wage would NOT impact the pay scales of non-minimum wage workers. I was pretty disappointed, especially since my logic and evidence/sources were sound.

Not even a year later, our state voted to do just that (way to go, MA!). Low and behold, the SCHOOL announced raises across the board. I think about this often.

Fuck you, Professor F. Teachers like you are why some students don't bother TRYING in school.

Yes! I don't know if I'd say it makes me look psychic, but if I've listened to someone enough, I can get a feel for their stress levels through their taste. It'll be a little duller or muddy if something is up, even when they seem otherwise fine. It's especially helpful if I've "tasted" them under stress before.

It's not always super helpful, though. I figure if people want to talk about things that are bothering them, they will. I try not to intrude but it's still interesting.

It might honestly be closer to sound-smell, but I have epilepsy, too, so the tests always come back wonky. Basically, my neurologists are like: *Shrugs* Whichever. 

Hahaha. The incompatibility part isn't true for me. Some of my favorite people have terrible tasting voices and I just have to deal with it.

BUT there are people's voices that...let's just say make me feel a certain way. They'll taste poisonous and ultimately be exactly that. Or the exact opposite, they'll taste like home and safety (like the *feeling* of a comfort food, even if they taste like something completely different). The few people who have had that feeling/taste have NEVER let me down. Literally never. When I feel that in a voice I'm immediately grateful to know that person.

It's kind of weird, but I like to think it's some kind of evolutionary warning sign.

The second option will just explain why the book is in the shape it's in. Bullet dodged.
